Heard on I.A. No.19063/2025, fifth application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
His earlier applications were dismissed as withdrawn.

2. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 20.09.2022 passed by 3rd Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge POCSO Act, Deasor, District Singrauli (M.P.) in Special Case No.
02/2020, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction U/s.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Imprisonment Fine In lieu of default 363 of IPC R.I. for 5 years Rs.1000/- Additional R.I. for 3 months 366 of IPC R.I. for 7 years Rs.1000/-
Additional R.I. for 3 months 376(1) of IPC R.I. for 10 years Rs.5000/- Additional R.I.
for 6 months 376(3) of IPC R.I. for 20 years Rs.5000/- Additional R.I. for 6 months 3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
It is submitted that the appellant has acquitted from the charges for the offence punishable under Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act.
It is further submitted that FSL report does not support the case of the prosecution, hence there is no medical evidence to connect the present appellant to the alleged crime.
The prosecutrix is a consenting party.
There is major variation of the statement of the prosecution witnesses.
The appellant has already undergone more than 3 years of incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2022 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
He is 2 CRA-9352-2022 ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
4. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: 6. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the fact that the FSL report does not support the case of the prosecution as well as the period of incarceration already undergone by the appellant, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant can be considered.
7. Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I.A. No.19063/2025 is allowed.

8 . It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 13.11.2025 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
9. List the matter for final hearing in due course.
